problem.text: Given that $\frac{1}{2!17!}+\frac{1}{3!16!}+\frac{1}{4!15!}+\frac{1}{5!14!}+\frac{1}{6!13!}+\frac{1}{7!12!}+\frac{1}{8!11!}+\frac{1}{9!10!}=\frac{N}{1!18!}$ find the greatest integer that is less than $\frac{N}{100}$.

steps.title: Where to start: the numbers in each denominator add to 19
steps.body: Look at the pairs of factorials: $2 + 17$, $3 + 16$, and so on up to $9 + 10$, and also $1 + 18$ on the right, all add to $19$. That is exactly the shape of a binomial coefficient, $\binom{19}{k} = \frac{19!}{k!\,(19-k)!}$. So multiply both sides of the equation by $19!$.

steps.title: Rewrite as binomial coefficients
steps.body:
After multiplying by $19!$, each fraction $\frac{19!}{k!\,(19-k)!}$ on the left becomes $\binom{19}{k}$, and the right side becomes $19N$:
$$\binom{19}{2} + \binom{19}{3} + \cdots + \binom{19}{9} = 19N.$$

your_turn.prompt: Which binomial coefficient does the term $\frac{19!}{5!\,14!}$ become?

steps.title: Use the whole row of Pascal's triangle
steps.body: The whole row adds to a power of two: $\binom{19}{0} + \binom{19}{1} + \cdots + \binom{19}{19} = 2^{19}$. By symmetry $\binom{19}{k} = \binom{19}{19-k}$, so the $20$ terms split into two equal halves, $k = 0$ to $9$ and $k = 10$ to $19$. Since $19$ is odd there is no middle term, so each half is $2^{18}$.

your_turn.prompt: Our sum starts at $k = 2$, not $k = 0$. What is $\binom{19}{0} + \binom{19}{1}$, the part we must remove from $2^{18}$?

steps.title: Solve for $N$
steps.body: So $19N = 2^{18} - 20$. Now find the number on the right and divide by $19$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Then $N = \frac{262124}{19} = 13796$, so $\frac{N}{100} = 137.96$. Careful: the problem asks for the greatest integer less than $\frac{N}{100}$, so round down, not to the nearest integer. The answer is **$137$**.
